newsitem.title: USA: AT&T reassigns U.S. billing executive - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: AT&T reassigns U.S. billing executive - WSJ.

text.p: AT&T Corp reassigned Ron Ponder, the executive who had supervised its attempt to build a new countrywide billing system, giving his job to a deputy who now oversees the company's communication network, the Wall Street Journal said in Monday's electronic edition.
Ponder, AT&T executive vice president and chief information officer, had drawn internal criticism for the company's problems with billings, the newspaper said.
His reassignment was announced on internal company electronic mail and confirmed by an AT&T spokesman, the Journal said.

Ponder, who the paper said could not be reached for comment, was given the job of forming a blueprint for making AT&T's global network and computer operations compatible with other partners, the newspaper said.
According to people at the company, AT&T President John Walter ordered the move early last week, the paper said.
Ponder would be replaced by Frank Ianna, a vice president and deputy.
